doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bebop, band changes and the road
title: Why he always keeps a guitar rather than piano
summary: Replacing cello in the group with Charles Lloyd and Albert Stinson, he explains that guitar's sustain suits his dancing style better than a keyboard.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Okay, so we jumped -- I was talking about the group that came right out of the quintet.
Oh, the group I had with Charles Lloyd and -­
Albert Stinson, (unintelligible), yeah, that group was -­
So you still have a guitar, you just got rid of the cello.

I found the guitar playing was very conducive to my playing, the sustaining power of the guitar as opposed to keyboard. Keyboard has no sustaining power, you know. The guitar can say (musical sound). He can hold a note for almost two bars -- I mean a sound.

Right, you dig. And since I dance I need that sustaining power as opposed to a keyboard would be choppy. An average keyboard player, a piano player, if he’s got this foot on the pedal, he’s not swinging, you know what I mean?
